functions.get_item(sku: str): returns dict {sku, name, unit_price, category} or None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id: str): returns dict {id, name, discount_rate, region} or None if id unknown; discount_rate is a fraction; region is a string code such as TX

why: Pricing module API: team money/percent convention, plus lookups that return None when nothing is found. Source CSVs store cents and whole-percent integers; pricing.py converts them.

pricing.discount_multiplier(cid): Decimal, e.g. 0.90 for 10% off, Decimal(1) if unknown customer

tax.tax_for(customer_id, lines, discount_mul: lines = [(sku, line_amount Decimal) for known items, before discount]; returns (tax_multiplier Decimal e.g. 1.0825, or 1 if no tax; tax_amount Decimal rounded to cent). tax.py decides which lines are taxable and on what base (after discount).

why: Proposal from agent3 (invoice). Lets invoice.py detect unknown SKUs and show tax % without knowing tax rules.

Units conflict with our team standard: money must be integer cents (1250 = 12.50 dollars) and percents must be percent numbers (10 = 10%). Float dollars and fraction rates cause cent-level rounding errors in tax (half-up rounding). Please change money to integer cents and percent to percent numbers. The None-for-not-found lookup behaviour is fine.

Same unit issue (Decimal dollars instead of integer cents). Also tax_for taking customer_id makes tax.py depend on pricing lookups. I suggest invoice passes region and discount_pct, and lines carry category (not sku). See proposal tax_api.

functions.tax_for(region, lines, discount_pct=0): region: customer region code string (e.g. TX) from pricing get_customer, or None if the customer is unknown (tax 0). lines: list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) for known items, before discount; category from pricing get_item. discount_pct: customer discount percent number (0 if none). Returns dict {taxable_cents, tax_pct, tax_cents}; tax_cents rounded half up to the cent. Raises KeyError if region is not in rates.csv.
functions.is_exempt(category): bool; True if the category is not taxed

why: Tax API from agent2 (tax). Uses the team cents/percent convention. Tax needs only region, discount and per-line category and amount, so tax.py does not depend on pricing; invoice.py passes them in. Returns the breakdown so invoice can show tax percent and amount.
Superseded: switching to integer cents and percent numbers as agent2 requested.
